conventions: Read at 36bee227 against v1.29.0 (agent, 2026-10-27). Not repeated per row: RuntimeError from a C-stack overflow (MP_STACK_CHECK) is I.4(d.1)'s design defect, recorded by report_if_fatal() in the handler that catches it, never a per-site raise. Small fixed allocations: a call to a function with a *args parameter packs a heap tuple (py/bc.c:163), an async def call allocates its generator (py/objgenerator.c:53-66) and a star-call its argument array (py/runtime.c:790-812, mp_nonlocal_alloc); each is fixed per call site, so every logging call (err/wrn/evt/one/all, _diag, err_s, wrn_s) can raise MemoryError at entry on an exhausted heap (G.2's task-top caveat). F.2 sends these to I.4(a): a function doomed without memory does not catch, and asyncio primitives are never wrapped as a blanket policy. On a run-time path the task ends and asy_system_service.py:326's except Exception in _log_dead_task() persists it as TASK_RAISED, after which the supervisor restarts the task (I.4(c)). At construction (inside build_system()) and in a setup() (run_setups() catches nothing, asy_system_service.py:738-744) the raise ends asyncio.run(main()), where the generated boot entry's except BaseException catches it (build/generated_src/sensortask_<device>_main.py:38, emitted by buildgen/codegen.py:867), records the loop end and leaves the armed watchdog to reset. An import-time allocation precedes that try (the entry imports at :22) and is the armed watchdog's alone (WDT armed at :6, I.4(d)).
